subject: Networking isolation & procurement sync — post-call summary
messages:
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novamed.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Chopra <priya@novamed.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:07:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up from today — isolation/topology constraints

Hi Ava / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo this morning. Quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can move procurement and architecture review along: 

- Business driver: regulator requires physical separation for patient-identifiable ML workflows; we need an option that keeps model inference inside our VPC or an on-prem enclave.
- Current constraint: our security team will not allow egress to multi-tenant public endpoints. All traffic must originate from our subnet and terminate inside our approved hosting zone.
- Performance expectation: 200 concurrent requests at p95 latency < 400ms for short text inference (avg token length ~60).
- Timeline: procurement window opens first week of March; decision by March 25 desired.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can support: dedicated VPC peering or a private deployment package that includes KMS integration and no outbound internet for inference nodes? Also please attach any minimal network diagram / port list that your infra team needs.

Attaching a rough topology sketch from our security lead (see attachment).

Sanjay Rao
Head of Engineering, Novamed Health

From: ava_chen@redwood.com <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novamed.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 18:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — isolation/topology constraints

Sanjay — thanks for the clear notes. Short answers and next steps below.

Recap of what we heard from your side:
- Regulatory driver: residency + air-gap-like constraints for PHI.
- Blocker: no outbound calls to multi-tenant hosted endpoints.
- Scale need: 200 concurrent short-text requests, ~60 tokens average, target p95 <400ms.

What Redwood can offer (initial):
- Private deployment (VPC or on-prem bundle) with customer-managed control plane and optional isolated inference nodes.
- KMS/HSM integration for key management and audit logs.
- Network modes: VPC peering, private link (cloud dependent), or fully air-gapped on-prem package for the most regulated customers.

Key dependencies / asks from Novamed to validate feasibility:
1) Public IP / outbound policy: confirm if peering + no-nat route acceptable vs strict air-gap.
2) Expected incoming throughput and steady-state qps across peak windows (please provide samples).
3) Procurement timeline and who owns L2/L3 network review (security or infra contact).

Next steps we propose:
- Ben will share a minimal port/list and an initial SOC2 excerpt that highlights our control surface.
- Redwood infra to produce a short feasibility note (network topology options and tradeoffs) by EOD tomorrow.
- Joint call the week of Mar 1 with your infra/security review board.

I'll attach the SOC2 excerpt and the port list Ben mentioned.

Thanks — Ava
Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood-soc2-brief.pdf
From: ben_carter@redwood.com <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay@novamed.com>, ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up from today — isolation/topology constraints

Sanjay / Ava — adding a slightly more technical view and an initial port/flow stub below. This is the minimal information our infra team needs to assess an isolated VPC deployment and estimate cost.

Minimal network requirements (initial):
- Outbound: none required from inference nodes if peered into customer's subnet.
- Ports: inbound from customer LB to inference nodes (TCP 443), internal health checks (TCP 8080), optional telemetry over a dedicated private channel (TCP 514/UDP 514 for syslog if you need it).
- NAT: avoid NAT for inference nodes; we prefer routing through a peered subnet or private link.
- DNS: customer-managed internal DNS or split-horizon is fine; we'll provide hostname mapping guidance.

Tradeoffs:
- VPC peering + route tables: faster to enable, lower cost. Leaves control plane connectivity decisions (we can use a small control-plane tunnel bound to customer-managed endpoints).
- Fully air-gapped on-prem: longer lead time, stricter procurement (hardware, install windows).

Proposal / ask for procurement calendar:
- Can Novamed accept a 'dedicated VPC deployment' contract (Redwood-managed inference nodes inside your VPC) with a small control-plane egress to a customer-approved bastion? If not, we will scope an on-prem bill of materials.
- Please confirm procurement decision-maker and budget band (so we can align our SOW options).

I'll prepare a short feasibility note and cost delta for peering vs on-prem and share by tomorrow EOB.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
attachments: none

Ava / Ben — internal alignment before the joint infra review: 

- I will draft the feasibility note (network topology + control-plane options) and include an appendix with SOC2 references.
- Ben: please include a short cost sketch for (a) VPC peering dedicated nodes, (b) private-link style option, (c) on-prem air-gap baseline. Keep the cost bands coarse — procurement just needs ballpark.
- Ava: schedule the March 2 joint call with Novamed security (10:00 PT looks good on their side). I'll attach the draft note in the morning for quick review.

We should not commit to an on-prem timeline until procurement confirms hardware lead times. Keep messaging: we can support their requirements, with tradeoffs and costs.

Naomi Feldman
Director, Solutions Architecture, Redwood Inference
